problem:
Which of the following systems of linear ODEs are decoupled?

- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=6{x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=4{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}$
- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=5{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-8{x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}$
- ${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}$
worked_solution:
A *decoupled system* consists of equations depending on only one variable, such as

$$
{x}_{i}^{′}(t)={\lambda }_{i}{x}_{i}(t),
$$

where ${\lambda }_{i}$ is a constant. This means that we can solve each equation independently. 

With this in mind, let's examine our systems.

- System I is *not* decoupled because some of its equations depend on more than one variable. For example, ${x}_{1}^{′}(t)=6{x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t)$ depends on ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t).$

- System II is decoupled since its equations depend on only one variable each. Indeed, ${x}_{1}^{′}(t)=5{x}_{1}(t)$ depends on only ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-8{x}_{2}(t)$ depends on only ${x}_{2}(t).$

- System III is *not* decoupled because some of its equations depend on more than one variable. For example, ${x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t)$ depends on ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".
